clue.text: Bug six groups occasionally

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: Roman numeral for six
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An infection that spreads through half a dozen groups now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is everyday slang for a virus or other minor infection.

clue.text: Spot rocket, possibly overhead where runners may be trained?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that is overhead sits above the other, so it is written first

blocks.note: rocket is a salad leaf, an example of a vegetable
a spot or small area

explanation.surface: Pick out a rocket in the sky above an athletics training track.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'overhead' puts the rocket piece above the spot. Runners are runner beans, climbing plants trained up canes, not athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable patch is a garden plot where runner beans are grown, their climbing stems tied in to supports.

clue.text: Essentially Terry Scott lobbied against Kenneth Williams?

definitions.note: a forename that goes with Williams, as Robin Williams

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its heart, so the central letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the centre letter of five
the centre letter of five
the centre letter of seven
the centre letter of seven
the centre letter of seven

explanation.surface: Did Carry On actor Terry Scott campaign against his co-star Kenneth Williams?
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Scott and Kenneth Williams were both British Carry On film comedians, so Kenneth Williams reads as one name; but Kenneth is wordplay and the definition is just Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Williams was the American comic actor, so Robin is a first name that can precede Williams.

clue.text: Clear TV star's last to split appearance money

indicators.note: splitting something opens it up so another letter can be wedged in between
the last of a word is its final letter, picked out here to go inside the other piece

blocks.note: a TV set
the final letter of star
the fee paid for appearing

explanation.surface: A television celebrity's last payment for showing up has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: Appearance money is a fee paid to a celebrity simply for turning up at an event.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone, as of a charge, is to release or liberate them.

clue.text: Evergreen musical with villain hiding two of the maidens

indicators.note: the villain is placed over the maidens, covering them up so they vanish and he stands where they were

blocks.note: the ABBA stage show Mamma Mia!
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over; two of them come out
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A long-running stage show featuring a villain who keeps some of the young women out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: CAD takes the place of the middle MM in MAMMA MIA, giving MA-CAD-AMIA. 'Evergreen' looks like praise for a long-running musical, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an evergreen tree from Australia, grown for its nuts, so it is an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Stupidly use most of milk for breakfast?

definitions.note: breakfast here means a breakfast food, an example

indicators.note: done stupidly means done without sense, so the letters end up in a muddled order
most of a word is all but a bit of it, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
the word minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Foolishly using up nearly all the milk for the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning, an example of a breakfast.

clue.text: John Bishop is ingesting new American drug

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the earlier pieces take the next letters inside them

blocks.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
chess notation for a bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: The comedian John Bishop is taking a new American narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bishop is a British stand-up comedian, so the name reads as one person; here 'John' and 'Bishop' are separate pieces, and the 'is' does double duty in the build.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the plant whose leaves and resin are smoked or eaten as a recreational narcotic.

clue.text: Thinking stand-up Jack will go on compering failing clubs

indicators.note: failing means lacking or without, so the letter for clubs is taken out

blocks.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian
MCing, acting as master of ceremonies
card-suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A comedian is considering hosting shows at struggling nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dee is a deadpan British comedian. In a down answer 'go on' puts his name on top of MCING with its C dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or consider, so deeming is a synonym of thinking in the sense of holding an opinion.

clue.text: Air statement wanting hospital department to reassemble bones

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the department's letters are missing from the fodder
reassembling means putting the parts together again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Make a public statement without the clinic so the broken bones can be set.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT happens to sit at the very end of 'statement', which makes the removal tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsi are the five long bones of the foot between the ankle and toes.

clue.text: Scandinavian band, after reforming, try adding cover of smash hit single

indicators.note: a band reforming gets back together in new form, so these letters are reshaped
a cover wraps the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a-ha, the Norwegian pop group
taken as written
taken as written
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Norwegian pop group gets back together and attempts a cover version of a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'adding' is itself part of the fodder alongside try and the outside of smash. A Hard Day's Night was a Beatles number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hard Day's Night was a 1964 Beatles record that topped the charts, a hit single.

clue.text: Agent upset to see GB News wasting seconds

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
wasting means losing or throwing away, so those letters are dropped from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second; plural, so both S letters go

explanation.surface: An operative is annoyed at having to watch a British TV news channel.
explanation.walkthrough: GB News is a British television news channel. Both S letters in 'see' and 'News' go before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary acting on behalf of others, which is one sense of agent.

clue.text: More are assuming Texas turns towards the Left

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the first word takes the state inside itself
in an across clue, turning to the left means reading from right to left, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
postal abbreviation for the US state of Texas

explanation.surface: More people are believing that the state of Texas is shifting politically leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The political reading of 'the Left' disguises a direction: in an across answer, towards the left means read backwards. 'Are' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, beyond the usual amount, which is a synonym of more.

clue.text: Shoot using 10 bore that's sawn-off

indicators.note: a sawn-off shotgun has its barrel cut short, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: the number written as a word, not a reference to entry 10
drill, a boring tool, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Fire a 10-bore sawn-off shotgun.
explanation.walkthrough: The '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it is just the number ten. Gun words (shoot, bore, sawn-off) all misdirect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender climbing growth from a plant stem, and shoot is a general word for new plant growth.

clue.text: A struggle to comprehend a time before Delta operated aircraft

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include or take in, so the struggle word holds the next letters inside

blocks.note: taken as written
to vie is to compete or strive
A as written plus T for time
D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An airline company had a hard time understanding an era before Delta Air Lines flew planes.
explanation.walkthrough: Delta is also a US airline, which makes it look part of the flying story; here it is just D, placed after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to fly or pilot an aeroplane, so aviated means flew or operated aircraft.

clue.text: Goat felt clumsy

blocks.note: a goat is something that butts, so cryptically a butter
felt in the sense of touched with the hand

explanation.surface: A goat felt awkward and ungainly.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words in 'Goat felt' change meaning: a goat is a creature that butts, and felt is the past of feel, not the cloth or an emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfingered describes someone who drops things, as if their hands were greasy, which is a form of clumsiness.

clue.text: Maybe East End boater's payment in kind

blocks.note: first meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for hat, and a boater is a straw hat
second meaning: retaliation matching what was done

explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney area of London, where rhyming slang swaps a word for a rhyming phrase; boater suggests someone in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the rhyming slang for a hat and the idiom for repaying an injury with the same.

clue.text: See 13
See 8
One who left post office career ultimately to pursue what's rightfully theirs?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is used

blocks.note: as in 'just deserts', what one deserves
the last letters of both words

explanation.surface: A worker left the Post Office career in the end to chase what they were owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post office' looks like one unit, but post belongs with the definition. In a down answer, 'pursue' puts the end letters below the deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter is a soldier who abandons their post or duty without permission.

clue.text: Perhaps cousins had more children

definitions.note: a verb phrase read cryptically as 'extended' plus its object 'family'

blocks.note: first meaning: relatives beyond parents and children, with cousins as an example
second meaning: read as a verb and object

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the phrase into a verb and its object: to have more children is to make the household bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Cousins, aunts and grandparents make up the wider circle of relations beyond the immediate household.

clue.text: Type of bomb – it isn't charged

blocks.note: first meaning: a nuclear weapon designed to release radiation
second meaning: a subatomic particle with no electric charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Isn't charged' sounds like a legal matter, someone not prosecuted, but it is physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron bomb is a kind of nuclear weapon, and a neutron is the uncharged particle in an atomic nucleus.

clue.text: See 18
Pure Northern Irish language elevating article

indicators.note: elevating means raising up, so in a down answer the article is lifted to the top

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Irish Gaelic
the indefinite article, already present in the language word

explanation.surface: A pure form of the Irish language in Northern Ireland that raises a point of grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: Write N then GAELIC, then lift its A up to the very top: A-N-GELIC. 'Northern Irish' reads as one phrase but splits into N and the Irish language.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, innocent and free of sin, which is to be pure.

clue.text: Appeal because of contract

blocks.note: a draw is an attraction, something with appeal
as in 'in that', introducing a reason

explanation.surface: A legal challenge arising from an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract is a verb here, to shrink, not the noun for an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: When the days draw in they grow shorter; to draw in is to pull inward or shrink, a sense of contract.

clue.text: Get kipper on inside of apron

indicators.note: the inside of a word is what is left once its outer letters are stripped away

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
to kipper fish is to cure it by salting and smoking

explanation.surface: Fetch a smoked herring and put it on the middle of your apron.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the kipper piece after the other. Kipper looks like a noun, the fish, but works as the verb for preserving it.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain or acquire it, a formal synonym of get.

clue.text: See 1
Government of revolutionary African country imprisoning this writer

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the country's name is read backwards
to imprison is to shut inside, so the country holds the writer within it

blocks.note: the West African state of Niger
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: A rebel African administration jails the author of the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government' and 'revolutionary' paint a coup, but the definition is the older sense of regimen as rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimen is an old word for rule or government, the same root as regime, though today it mostly means a prescribed routine.

clue.text: State of blue whale's tail

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the blue is the sea, as is the main
the final letter

explanation.surface: The condition of a blue whale's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue whale' reads as one animal, but blue is the sea (the main) and only the end of whale is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is one of the US states, in New England.

clue.text: School Trust Board's odd characters

indicators.note: the odd characters are those in first, third, fifth position and so on, counting along the words

blocks.note: letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of TRUSTBOARD

explanation.surface: The governing body of an academy trust is full of strange people.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd here means the odd-numbered letters, not strange people; count across both words ignoring the space. School is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, which is what a tutor does as a verb.

clue.text: Absorbent material in contact with outpouring

blocks.note: as in 'cheek to cheek', touching
welling up is pouring or rising out

explanation.surface: A soaking fabric touched by a flood of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Towelling is the thick looped cotton fabric used for towels because it soaks up water well.

clue.text: Accident with work going on strike

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece going on another is attached after it

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
and joins things together, as with does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going on' places the work word after the others in this across answer. Strike suggests a union walkout, but it is just a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road accident where the driver who causes it leaves without stopping.

clue.text: Chisel polish off both taps initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters, the first of each word

blocks.note: a pair of taps are cold and hot, and their first letters are taken
to polish off food is to eat it all up

explanation.surface: Use a carpenter's tool and finish smoothing the woodwork round the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both taps' are the hot and cold taps of a basin, so C and H; the clue's own word order puts the eating first but the taps come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To chisel someone is informal slang for swindling or cheating them out of something.
